but from thirst also they were hard pressed through the lack of rain;

And there was a pestilence in India and in the whole of Persia;
forty thousand biers of the dead were brought out from Isfahan in a single week.
And in Baghdad, moreover, not a house was left in which there was no wailing.
And in Mosul four thousand children died of the disease of croup {OCR?}.
And in the year 425
425 of the Arabs [= 1033/1034 AD],
which is the year 1345
1345 of the Greeks [= 1033/1034 AD]:
a violent and vehement wind blew in the month of Kanun in Nisibis,
and it uprooted the majority of the olive, mulberry, and jujube trees,
and it overturned even buildings of stone and lime.
And after it came a heavy rain,
and much hail fell resembling hands, braziers, and fingers.
And there was an earthquake in Egypt and in Palestine;
and people went out from the houses
and remained under the open sky for eight days.
And half of the city of Balash fell.
And the earth swallowed up many villages in Syria with their inhabitants.
And parts of the capitals {OCR?} of the Temple of Jerusalem fell down,
and the minaret of the Arabs in Ashkelon,
and the top of the minaret of Gaza,
and half of Acre.
And the sea retreated about three parasangs,
and people entered to collect fish and snails;
and the waters returned
and drowned some of them.
And in the month of Shebat there was seen the likeness of a pillar of light in the zodiac sign of the Ear of Corn (Virgo),
from evening until morning,
for many days,
from the synod (conjunction/new moon) until the full moon.
And after [some] days,
a shooting star fell like a great flash of lightning,
and the whole land of Sen'ar was filled with its light.
And many of the simple people thought
that the sky was torn apart.
And there was a pestilence in Baghdad,
and about seventy thousand people died of the disease of choking (quinsy).
And after a year,
violent winds blew upon the Persian Sea (the Gulf),
and more than fifty ships were sunk,
and two thousand and five hundred people were drowned.
And the sea and the rivers overflowed,
and the floodgates of heaven were opened with abundant rain,
and the waters covered most of the villages.
It is said
that some people, after having escaped on planks and decks of ships from the drowning of the sea and reached the dry land,
a flood met them
and turned them back again
